framework-parity.name: Framework parity
framework-parity.definition: Agreement between corresponding computations under a stated numerical contract.
framework-parity.explanation: A port can produce plausible predictions while changing weight layout, bias broadcasting, or loss reduction. Parity checks fix data, parameters, dtype, shapes, and optimization settings, then compare intermediate quantities in order. This chapter checks forward output before gradients, one update, and restored inference. Absolute and relative tolerances account for bounded rounding after equivalent operations; they must not conceal nonfinite values or a different mathematical function. A passing affine fixture does not validate every model in a framework.

autodiff-backend.name: Differentiable backend
autodiff-backend.definition: An execution backend augmented with automatic differentiation of recorded operations.
autodiff-backend.explanation: The optional Burn program wraps its CPU ndarray backend in an Autodiff decorator. Trainable tensors request gradients before the forward computation, and backward returns a container from which individual derivatives are retrieved. These derivatives do not update parameters automatically. The example applies explicit SGD to the inner weight and bias tensors after obtaining both gradients. This separation makes the mathematical comparison visible and avoids confusing differentiation, device execution, and optimizer state as one operation.

runtime-interchange.name: Runtime interchange
runtime-interchange.definition: Moving a specified computation and its state between execution implementations.
runtime-interchange.explanation: Weights alone do not describe a portable model. An interchange contract identifies architecture, shapes, layout, dtype, preprocessing, and supported operations. The active lab uses an eight-byte S09AFF01 marker followed by eight little-endian f64 values for a non-square affine layer, totaling 72 bytes. An independent runtime adapts the layout and checks forward, gradient, and update parity. The optional preserved Burn program has its own two-by-two fixture and format; it does not import this new file. Neither format is an ONNX graph or a general training-resume checkpoint.
